newsitem.title: UK: UK's soccer league says no pay-per-view TV talks.
newsitem.headline: UK's soccer league says no pay-per-view TV talks.

text.p: English soccer's Premier League said on Thursday that official talks had not yet begun on the introduction of pay-per-view broadcasts of matches.
Shares in English champions Manchester United added 19p to 525p on Thursday following a report in The Independent nespaper that pay-per-view matches could begin next year.

"The position remains that there is an option for the introduction of pay-per-view in the current contract and in the new agreement which starts next year," a Premier League spokesman said. He added that official negotiations to introduce pay-per-view were not yet underway.
The Independent report said that BSkyB executives were holding informal talks with several leading clubs about the introduction of pay-per-view.
Pay television operator BSkyB recently signed a new deal to retain the live rights to English soccer until 2001.
BSkyB shows individual matches live on Sunday afternoons and Monday evenings but is believed to want to make the whole Saturday afternoon programme avaiable on a pay-per-view basis.
That would become possible once BSkyB launches digital satellite with up to 200 channels late next year.

Top teams in the 20-club Premier League are keen to tap into the potential riches offered by pay-per-view which reports suggest could be priced at 10 stg per match. But some of the smaller clubs are nervous about its impact on gate receipts.
Pay-per-view soccer has already been introduced in France and Italy and BSkyB has experimented with pay-per-view in Britain with two heavyweight boxing events.
